headline: Blue Jays edge Phillies in series opener, 5-4
recap: The Phillies fell to the Toronto Blue Jays 5-4 in Friday night's series opener at Citizens Bank Park. The teams traded runs early and were tied 2-2 after three innings, but single runs by Toronto in the fourth, sixth and eighth put the Blue Jays up 5-2 before Philadelphia scored twice in the ninth to close within one. Andres Gimenez and Josh Smith each homered for Toronto, with Smith going 3-for-4 with three runs scored. Zack Wheeler took the loss, allowing four earned runs over 5.1 innings, and Tyler Rogers worked around three walks in the ninth for Toronto's save. Bryce Harper drove in two runs, and Kyle Schwarber and Justin Crawford each doubled for the Phillies.
The loss dropped Philadelphia to 62-55, second in the NL East, 8.5 games behind the division-leading Atlanta Braves (70-46), and snapped what had been a one-game winning streak.

The Phillies continue the series against Toronto on Saturday, first pitch 6:05 PM ET at Citizens Bank Park. Aaron Nola starts for Philadelphia against Blue Jays right-hander Max Scherzer. DraftKings has the Phillies as -153 moneyline favorites.
